correctness.rationale: From the published Floquet coefficients, the determinant is exactly affine in \(Q=\cos\theta_1+\cos\theta_2\) with coefficient \(2k(k^2-1)\sin(k\ell)\). Positive point spectrum requires the fiber equation on a positive-measure quasimomentum set, forcing that coefficient to vanish. The branch \(\sin(k\ell)=0\) gives \(4k^2\sin(2\mu)\), nonzero for \(0<\mu<\pi/2\); the remaining \(k=1\) branch reduces exactly to \(4\sin(2(\mu+\ell))\). Conversely this vanishing makes every fiber singular at \(k=1\), yielding infinite multiplicity in the direct integral. The bundled checker independently reconstructs these identities on deterministic test grids.

value.rationale: The source emphasizes that interior phase destroys the infinite endpoint flat-band series but leaves open whether other point spectrum survives, giving one \(k=1\) example. The result turns that example into a complete positive point-spectrum classification over the full two-parameter family \((\ell,\mu)\): generically there is no positive point spectrum, while a codimension-one resonance supports exactly one infinitely degenerate level. This is a natural structural boundary for transport and flat-band persistence, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
